entries.title: Jeremiah 37:1
segments:
vv 1-3. 
 
To consult God's servants can profit us nothing, unless we obey the counsels which they deliver to us in his name.

entries.title: Jeremiah 37:5
segments:
vv 5-10. 
 
While men continue to practise iniquity, all their plans to obtain deliverance and salvation through their fellow sinners will prove vain.

entries.title: Jeremiah 37:11
segments:
vv 11-15. 
 
Hatred and prejudice make men ready to entertain unfounded suspicious against their neighbors, and to construe as crimes their most innocent acts.

entries.title: Jeremiah 37:12
segments:
To separate himself thence; or, according to some, to take his portion thence; that is, to receive from his patrimony in Anathoth what belonged to him. 
 
  In the midst of the people; along with the rest of the people.

entries.title: Jeremiah 37:13
segments: Fallest away to the Chaldeans; his predictions of the success of the Chaldeans, and his exhortations to the people to submit to their yoke, gave plausibility to this slander.

entries.title: Jeremiah 37:17
segments: Wicked men are often driven in their distress to seek counsel from those whom they are afraid openly to countenance and protect.

entries.title: Jeremiah 37:19
segments: False teachers may flatter their patrons with the hope of impunity in sin, but they cannot help them in the day of trouble.

entries.title: Jeremiah 37:20
segments:
vv 20-21. 
 
Whatever perils and sufferings come upon us in the discharge of our duty, we should meet with courage and alacrity.  At the same time, we ought to use all proper means to avoid needless exposure, since suffering for its own sake has neither goodness nor merit.
